disease_label_per_paper: Aplastic anemia induced by human parvovirus B19 infection in an immunocompetent adult male
presentation_summary: 22-year-old immunocompetent man presented with periumbilical abdominal pain for one week, watery stools for two days, fever with chills and rigor for one day, fatigue, and weakness.
Examination showed pallor, stable vital status, and no rash, joint pain, organomegaly, or lymphadenopathy reported.
Initial evaluation showed anemia, thrombocytopenia, profound neutropenia, relative lymphocytosis, and an inappropriately low reticulocyte response for the degree of anemia.

risk_context.source_text_value: Human parvovirus B19 IgM and molecular testing were positive during workup.
The patient was described as immunocompetent and had no comorbidities.

quality_warnings: White blood cell count in the published table is internally ambiguous in extracted text, so ANC and differential were preserved but WBC was not used for ranking.
Parvovirus testing, marrow biopsy, smear interpretation, final diagnosis, treatment response, and outcome are confirmatory or course data and excluded from presentation-only ranking.
